Differential Diagnosis of PD, PSP, and MSA: An XGBoost Approach to Retinal Layer Analysis

M. Rodriguez-Rubio2, F. J. Martínez-Murcia*1,2, J. E. Arco3, I. A. Illán1,2, F. Segovia1,2, C. Jiménez-Mesa2, C. Vázquez-García2,1, J.M. Górriz1,2, J. Ramírez1,2, S. Schönecker4, S. Kamp4, L. Klatte4, S. Katzdobler4, L. Marth4, O. Wagemann4, C. Palleis4, U. Fietzek4, E. Weidinger4, A. Danek4, G. Hölinger4, J. Havla4, A. Bernhardt4, A. Jäck4, J. Levin4

1Dpt. Signal Theory, Networking and Communications,University of Granada, Granada (Spain); 2Andalusian Research Institute in Data Science and Computational Intelligence (DaSCI), Granada (Spain); 3Mind, Brain and Behavior Research Center (CIMCYC), Granada (Spain); 4Department of Neurology, LMU University Hospital,Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Munich (Germany)

1. Introduction

  • Clinical Challenge: Parkinson’s disease (PD), progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP), and multiple system atrophy (MSA) share overlapping clinical presentations in early stages, making differential diagnosis challenging.

  • Underlying Proteinopathies: PD and MSA are characterized by alpha-synuclein aggregation (synucleinopathies), whereas PSP involves pathological tau deposition (tauopathy).

  • The Retina as a Window to the CNS: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) enables precise, non-invasive quantification of individual retinal layers, reflecting pathology-specific thinning patterns.

  • Objective: We present a systematic machine learning evaluation using XGBoost across four classification tasks to distinguish healthy controls, proteinopathic groups, and clinical subtypes from OCT retinal morphometry.

2. Methodology

Macular records were acquired and segmented using the Heidelberg Spectralis OCT device. Last higher-quality visits per patient were included, averaging both eyes to represent bilateral neurodegenerative involvement. A total of 29 morphometric features were extracted, normalized at the subject level by total macular volume (TMV + Z), and standardized (Z-score).

2.2 CLASSIFICATION FRAMEWORK (XGBOOST)

Classification was conducted using the eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) algorithm , trained on the 29 morphometric features plus derived features (ratios between adjacent retinal layers and global-vs-sector differences). Four tasks of increasing difficulty were addressed: HC vs. rest, PD+MSA vs. PSP, PD/PSP/MSA, and the four classes simultaneously. Performance was evaluated via repeated 5-fold stratified cross-validation (10 × 5-fold CV), which preserves class proportions in every fold and reduces the variance of the estimate on a small cohort. Eye averaging and TMV normalization were applied before the data split, while feature scaling was fitted only on the training data of each fold to prevent information leakage. Models were compared using accuracy, balanced accuracy (main selection metric, robust to class imbalance) and macro-averaged F1. Feature relevance was assessed with XGBoost gain and SHAP values.

2.1 DATASET AND PARTICIPANTS

From 488 initial records (186 participants), individuals with low-quality estimations or missing values were discarded, resulting in 134 subjects:

Group N Age (mean±SD) M/F
HC 36 63.6 ± 9.9 20 / 33
PD 46 59.5 ± 13.0 29 / 19
PSP 34 70.4 ± 7.5 20 / 17
MSA 18 59.0 ± 7.6 20 / 9

Nine macular layers were segmented (RNFL, GCL, IPL, INL, OPL, ONL, RPE), alongside inner/outer retinal layer aggregates (IRL, ORL), total macular volume (TMV), ETDRS grid ring zones, and the RNFL-to-NT ratio.

3. Results

4. Key findings

  • Robust Biological Stratification ( ≈ 70%): The XGBoost framework effectively distinguishes synucleinopathies (PD+MSA) from tauopathies (PSP) (0.704 ± 0.057), comparable to binary HC vs. pathology discrimination (0.724 ± 0.079).
  • Divergent Retinal Signatures: Findings confirm that alpha-synuclein and tau pathology exert divergent neurodegenerative pressures on inner and outer retinal architecture.
  • Multiclass Phenotypic Overlap: Performance in 3-class (0.521) and 4-class (0.395) settings highlights the significant morphological and clinical overlap between PD and MSA.
  • Clinical Translation: Combining OCT biomarkers with machine learning paves the way for faster, non-invasive, and cost-effective early-stage stratification in atypical parkinsonism.
